hero.title: US–Iran Talks Continue as Oil Climbs Above $106 and Global Markets Face Fresh Pressure
hero.description: Diplomatic efforts involving the United States and Iran continue through mediators, while uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz keeps oil prices and global markets under pressure.

breaking: 🚨 US–Iran: Separate talks through mediators continue as Washington and Tehran explore a possible route towards ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
🛢️ Oil: Brent crude rises to around $106.77 a barrel as concerns over Middle Eastern supply disruptions continue.
⚡ Energy: Qatar-linked LNG vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has increased, although security risks remain.
🇳🇬 Nigeria: Domestic refining and fuel supply remain major economic issues as international oil prices rise.
🇳🇬 Nigeria: The 2027 AFCON qualifying campaign continues, with Nigeria having opened its campaign with a 2–1 win over Madagascar.
🌍 DR Congo: The Ebola outbreak has surpassed 8,000 confirmed cases, with 3,901 reported deaths as of 26 September.
🇿🇦 South Africa: Two separate shootings over the weekend left at least 27 people dead, according to police and Reuters reporting.
🇪🇺 Europe: Energy prices and winter supply remain major concerns as governments monitor the impact of the Middle East crisis.
🇺🇦 Ukraine: European governments continue discussions on support for Ukraine and measures targeting Russia's sanctions-busting networks.
🇦🇺 Australia: The Reserve Bank is due to announce its latest interest-rate decision amid persistent inflation concerns.
📉 Markets: US Treasury yields have climbed to multi-year highs while Asian shares face pressure from rising oil prices and borrowing costs.

featured.title: US–Iran Diplomacy Continues as Hormuz Crisis Keeps Global Energy Markets on Edge
featured.content: US and Iranian officials are continuing separate discussions through mediators in a renewed attempt to find a way out of the seven-month conflict. The latest discussions centre on an updated Iranian proposal involving the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, sanctions and economic restrictions, and renewed nuclear negotiations. No final agreement has been reached. Meanwhile, Brent crude rose to about $106.77 a barrel on Tuesday as markets continued to price in supply risks linked to the conflict.

articles.title: US–Iran Talks Continue Through Mediators
articles.content: US and Iranian officials held separate discussions with mediators as efforts continued towards a possible agreement to end the conflict. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran was awaiting a US response to a proposal that includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for measures including an end to hostilities, economic relief and renewed nuclear talks. President Donald Trump has said he rejected the earlier version of the proposal, while further negotiations are expected. No comprehensive settlement has been confirmed.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran talks diplomacy New York Strait Hormuz

articles.title: Oil Climbs Above $106 as Hormuz Risk Remains
articles.content: Brent crude rose about 1.4% to $106.77 a barrel on Tuesday, while US West Texas Intermediate increased to around $93.94. The rise reflects continued concern over disruption to energy supplies linked to the US–Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz. Higher oil prices can feed into transport, manufacturing, food and household energy costs.

articles.title: Some Qatar-Linked LNG Traffic Resumes Through Hormuz
articles.content: Shipping data indicates that LNG traffic linked to Qatar has increased through the Strait of Hormuz despite the continuing conflict. Several QatarEnergy-linked vessels have resumed visible movements after reduced activity caused by security concerns. The increase suggests some energy flows are recovering, although the security situation remains unpredictable.

articles.title: Nigeria Keeps Domestic Refining and Fuel Supply in Focus
articles.content: Nigeria continues to place greater emphasis on domestic crude refining as international energy prices remain elevated. The Dangote Refinery remains central to discussions about domestic fuel supply and Nigeria's wider energy security. Rising global crude prices nevertheless continue to influence the country's fuel market, government revenues and broader economic conditions.

articles.title: Nigeria Starts AFCON 2027 Qualifying Campaign With Victory
articles.content: Nigeria opened its 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 2–1 victory over Madagascar. Nigeria came from behind after Madagascar scored first, with George Ilenikhena equalising before Moses Usor completed the turnaround. The Super Eagles face Guinea-Bissau next, with Victor Osimhen unavailable for the opening qualifiers while recovering from a muscle injury.

articles.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 8,000 Confirmed Cases
articles.content: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 8,000 confirmed cases, with 3,901 reported deaths as of 26 September, according to figures reported by health authorities and AP. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus strain, is putting significant pressure on the healthcare system. WHO and Africa CDC teams are supporting containment efforts while health workers face shortages, insecurity and community resistance. The figures are developing and may change as new cases are confirmed.
articles.imageQuery: Ebola response healthcare workers Democratic Republic Congo

articles.title: South Africa Investigates Two Deadly Mass Shootings
articles.content: South African police are investigating two separate shootings that left at least 27 people dead over the weekend. Reuters reported that 18 people were killed in a tavern shooting in Wedela near Johannesburg, while another 10 people were killed in Lwandle near Cape Town. Investigators are pursuing suspects and examining possible organised-crime and business-related motives. Authorities have not established a single explanation for the two attacks.
articles.imageQuery: South Africa police shooting investigation Johannesburg

articles.title: Europe Watches Energy Prices and Winter Supply Risks
articles.content: European governments continue to monitor energy markets as Middle Eastern supply disruptions put additional pressure on prices. Higher energy costs can affect households, transport operators and energy-intensive industries. EU policymakers are also discussing measures to manage gas demand and protect energy security as winter approaches.
articles.imageQuery: Europe energy market gas pipelines winter

articles.title: EU Maintains Pressure on Russia Over Ukraine
articles.content: European governments continue to support Ukraine while tightening measures against Russia. EU countries recently imposed sanctions on 10 individuals and 17 entities over the deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia. The Russia–Ukraine war continues to affect European security, energy policy and government spending.
articles.imageQuery: European Union Ukraine flags Brussels diplomacy

articles.title: Global Bond Yields Rise as Markets Reassess Inflation and Interest Rates
articles.content: Global financial markets are under pressure as rising oil prices and government bond yields increase concerns about inflation and borrowing costs. The US 10-year Treasury yield reached around 5.27%, its highest level in about 19 years, while Asian equity markets were generally weaker. Higher sovereign yields can raise financing costs for governments, companies and households.
articles.imageQuery: global financial markets stock exchange bond yields

articles.title: Gold Holds Near Seven-Week Low
articles.content: Spot gold remained around $4,124 an ounce early Tuesday, close to a seven-week low, as investors assessed higher oil prices and expectations that interest rates could remain elevated. Higher yields can reduce the appeal of assets such as gold that do not generate interest.

articles.title: Technology Markets Face Pressure From Higher Rates and US–China Tensions
articles.content: Technology shares are facing a more complicated market environment as higher borrowing costs and continuing US–China technology tensions affect investor sentiment. Markets are also watching potential restrictions involving Chinese technology components and the cost of financing major artificial-intelligence infrastructure projects.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence technology semiconductor stock market

articles.title: Australia Interest-Rate Decision in Focus
articles.content: The Reserve Bank of Australia is due to announce its September monetary-policy decision on Tuesday. Financial markets and economists have widely expected a 25-basis-point increase to 4.60%, from 4.35%, as policymakers respond to persistent inflation pressures. The final decision and accompanying guidance will determine how markets assess the next steps for Australian interest rates.
articles.imageQuery: Reserve Bank of Australia Sydney building

articles.title: Asia Markets Feel Pressure From Oil and Rising Bond Yields
articles.content: Asian equity markets are beginning Tuesday under pressure as investors respond to higher oil prices and a global bond sell-off. Japan, South Korea and Australia are among the markets affected by higher borrowing costs, while currencies remain sensitive to expectations about central-bank policy.

morningSummary: The global agenda this Tuesday is dominated by the continuing US–Iran conflict and efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices have risen above $106 a barrel, although some Qatar-linked LNG traffic through the waterway is showing signs of recovery. Nigeria is balancing domestic refining and fuel-supply concerns with the wider impact of international crude prices. In Africa, Nigeria has begun its AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign with a win, while the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 8,000 confirmed cases. South Africa is investigating two deadly mass shootings. Europe remains concerned about energy prices and winter supply, while financial markets are under pressure from rising bond yields. Australia is also in focus ahead of its latest interest-rate decision.
bigQuestion: With energy prices rising and global tensions continuing, how much longer can governments shield ordinary people from the economic impact?
quoteOfTheDay: When the world feels uncertain, stay calm, stay informed and remember that wise decisions are often made by those who take the time to understand before they act.
